Compile regular expressions

Source: R/compile.R
re_compile.Rd

re_compile() compiles each pattern once, with PCRE2's just-in-time compiler where the platform allows it, and returns an re vector that every re_*() function accepts in place of a character pattern. Compilation goes through the pattern cache, so compiling the same pattern again is cheap; see re_cache_size().

Usage

re_compile(
  pattern,
  flags = "",
  dialect = c("pcre", "js"),
  literal = FALSE,
  jit = TRUE
)

Arguments

pattern

A character vector of regular expressions. NA gives an NA element.

flags

A single string of flag letters, applied to every pattern:

LetterMeaning
iCase-insensitive.
m^ and $ match at line boundaries.
s. matches a newline.
xIgnore whitespace and allow # comments.
xxAs x, and also ignore whitespace inside character classes.
nOnly named groups capture.
UQuantifiers are lazy unless followed by ?.
JGroups may share a name.
u\w, \d, \b and POSIX classes follow Unicode properties.
rNo case equivalence between ASCII and non-ASCII characters.
aD, aS, aWKeep \d, \s or \w ASCII under u.
aT, aPKeep POSIX digit classes, or all POSIX classes, ASCII under u.
aAll five a restrictions.

Each letter may appear once, and x and xx exclude each other.

dialect

"pcre", the default, compiles patterns as base R's perl = TRUE does. "js" adds the options node-pcre2 uses for JavaScript patterns: \u escapes, $ only at the very end, and unset back-references that match the empty string.

literal

If TRUE, each pattern is matched as a literal string, with no metacharacters. Only the flags i and r apply to a literal.

jit

If TRUE, JIT-compile each pattern when the platform allows it. If JIT compilation fails, the interpreter is used and re_info()$jit is FALSE.

Value

An re vector, as long as pattern.

See also

re_info() to inspect compiled patterns, re_escape() to quote metacharacters.

Examples

re <- re_compile(c("(\\d+)-(\\d+)", "^[a-z]+$"), flags = "i")
re
#> <re[2]>
#> [1] /(\d+)-(\d+)/i
#> [2] /^[a-z]+$/i
re_info(re)
#>         pattern flags dialect literal groups group_names  jit min_length prefix
#> 1 (\\d+)-(\\d+)     i    pcre   FALSE      2          ,  TRUE          3       
#> 2      ^[a-z]+$     i    pcre   FALSE      0             TRUE          1       
#>   backrefs pcre2_version
#> 1    FALSE         10.48
#> 2    FALSE         10.48

# A literal pattern needs no escaping
re_compile("1+1=2", literal = TRUE)
#> <re[1]>
#> [1] /1+1=2/ (literal)
